name: walgit
description: walgit: a git host where object storage holds the write-ahead log and is the source of truth, and the bare repo on local disk is a disposable cache rebuildable from the log (ADR-0007 in the zbc repository, docs/adr/)
instructions: STATUS: the front door and the push path are deployable — a Fly machine serving git over SSH (:22, raw TCP) and smart-HTTP (:443), with every push persisted to the write-ahead log in object storage before it is acknowledged and linearized by compare-and-swap on index.json. The bare repos on the machine's filesystem are a cache, reconciled against the log on every access and materialized from it when the objects a ref needs are absent. A repo whose cache is gone is rebuilt from the log on first access — not disaster recovery but the normal path, since the machine stops whenever it is idle. NOT yet done: compaction/orphan collection — a rejected push leaves an uploaded pack that findOrphans can recover but nothing yet reclaims. walgit runs on Fly rather than Cloudflare because it serves git over SSH and no Cloudflare product delivers raw inbound TCP to a Worker or Container (see docs/adr/0006 in the zbc repository). Requires FLY_API_TOKEN (a personal access token, not a deploy token), plus: WALGIT_SSH_HOST_KEY (an ed25519 private key — `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f walgit_host -N ''`; it must be a secret because the container filesystem does not survive a machine stop and a regenerated host key trips every client's man-in-the-middle warning), WALGIT_SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEYS (newline-separated public keys; each is pinned to a forced command server-side), WALGIT_HTTP_TOKENS (comma-separated bearer tokens; git sends them as the Basic-auth password), and the log's home: WALGIT_S3_ENDPOINT, WALGIT_S3_BUCKET, WALGIT_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and WALGIT_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from an r2 module instance's S3-API credentials. Without those four the host still serves reads from its local cache but REFUSES every push — accepting one it cannot persist is the single failure this app exists to prevent. The fly instance MUST set ipv4: "dedicated" — SSH is on port 22 and shared IPv4 covers 80/443 only, a difference `fly deploy` does not report.
